answer: Separated beacon timing attestation admits an identity only when one device records arrival times from three fixed radio beacons fitting a single physical point; a clone cannot appear on both sides of a dune ridge at once because signals obey light speed. The verifier rejects traces whose implied positions differ beyond clock error. Each identity needs its own receiver, power, and distinct mounting ledge at least 250 m from others; an attacker pays hardware and site access per identity. A quill-marked paper tape kept by each site anchors the audit.
